svg.title: Warrigal greens and bower spinach stop check before preparation
svg.desc: Working two-part comparison prompt, not an identification key or eating clearance. Leaves alone are not enough. Follow the same plant from overall growth, to flower attachment, to mature fruit. Warrigal greens are a low sprawling herb with flowers at or very near a leaf node and a roughly one-centimetre dry or thinly succulent fruit with angles, wings or short horns. Bower spinach is a trailing or climbing woody-based plant with yellow flowers on visible slender stalks about five to thirty millimetres long and a five-to-eight-millimetre fruit that is fleshy outside and hard within. A source-labelled Victorian photograph now shows attached red and yellow-orange bower-spinach fruit, but it has no ruler and mature stage is not independently confirmed. The guide still lacks a matched, measured mature-fruit pair. If flower attachment and mature fruit cannot both be checked on the same plant, stop: do not taste, eat or prepare it. Never transfer the Warrigal boiling method to bower spinach. The percentages shown estimate source wording and new layout completeness only, not correct identification, food safety or survival.
svg.text: WARRIGAL GREENS OR BOWER SPINACH?
WORKING STOP CHECK · PART 1 OF 2
NOT AN IDENTIFICATION KEY OR EATING CLEARANCE
Subjective estimates: source wording 95%; new layout 60%.
These are not probabilities of correct identity, food safety or survival.
Use the photographs and both parts together. Expert review is still required.
LEAVES ALONE ARE NOT ENOUGH
Do not taste or prepare either plant from a leaf match.
FOLLOW ONE PLANT THROUGH THREE CHECKS
whole growth
flower attachment
mature
fruit
WARRIGAL GREENS
• low, sprawling herb
• flower at or very near a leaf node
• fruit about 1 cm; dry or thinly fleshy,
with angles, wings or short horns
BOWER SPINACH
• trailing or climbing; woody at base
• yellow flower on a 5–30 mm stalk
• fruit 5–8 mm; fleshy outside,
hard within
WORKING DRAFT — CONTINUE TO PART 2 BEFORE ANY PREPARATION
STOP UNLESS THE WHOLE CHECK AGREES
WORKING STOP CHECK · PART 2 OF 2
CURRENT PHOTO LIMIT
No matched, measured mature-fruit pair is in this guide.
Bower photo: no ruler; maturity is not expert-confirmed.
STOP IF ANY ANSWER IS NO OR UNSURE
□ Did you follow the same plant from habit to reproductive parts?
□ Can you see where its flower joins and whether it has a stalk?
□ Is mature fruit present and consistent with the botanical account?
IF A CHECK IS MISSING OR INCONSISTENT
Do not taste it. Do not eat it. Do not prepare it.
Never transfer the Warrigal boiling method to bower spinach.
Use carried food or another already-known, approved option.
Botanical basis: VicFlora and Flora of Australia (S-342, S-400).
No Traditional Owner name, food method or permission is inferred on this card.
Botanist, food-safety and novice no-consumption review remain outstanding.
WORKING DRAFT — IF UNSURE, DO NOT EAT
